actionability.rationale: An author can generally select, construct, validate, and reject each treatment using concrete conditions and platform instructions.

concision.rationale: The material is dense but usually earns its detail through executable constraints, explicit ownership, or acceptance criteria. A few local rules are repeated after already being established.

nonRedundancy.rationale: Ownership and links are unusually disciplined. A small number of repeated local restatements can be removed without losing usable context.

specificity.rationale: Guidance consistently names inputs, states, fit gates, fallbacks, and rejection conditions. One statistical-admission rule remains underspecified.

findings.excerpt: Use `disc-chevron` for a repeated description-to-consequence row by default... The preferred implication treatment is the filled `disc-chevron`...
findings.reason: The preferred-default rule is stated twice with nearly identical meaning in the same owner.
findings.recommendedChange: Keep the selection rule as canonical and shorten the acceptance bullet to verification that the selected registered variant is used consistently.

findings.excerpt: Show at most five group rows... Reject more than five rows... Show at most five rows.
findings.location: Group selection and ordering; Failure modes; Acceptance test
findings.reason: The five-row cap is repeated three times in one chart owner without adding a distinct exception or verification detail.
findings.recommendedChange: Retain the construction rule and the acceptance verification; remove the duplicate failure-mode repetition.

findings.excerpt: Add a trend line only when the data type and sample support the named fitting method; report its basis or diagnostic...
findings.reason: The required diagnostic is named but no admissible criterion is required, leaving authors to guess when a fitted line is sufficiently supported.
findings.recommendedChange: Require the plan to declare the fitting method and its acceptance basis, such as a pre-specified analytical rationale, sample threshold, or diagnostic criterion, before rendering the line.

findings.excerpt: Add one interpretation or definition when the metric is a ratio, proxy, threshold result, nonstandard unit, or otherwise lacks a self-evident denominator.
findings.reason: “Self-evident denominator” is subjective and can lead to inconsistent omission of material bases across otherwise comparable metric fields.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace the catch-all with a testable rule: include the denominator or basis unless it is printed in the value, label, subtitle, or shared exhibit note.

judgement.summary: All manifest files were reviewed. The guidance is highly specific, operational, and consistently owned; the four findings are small copy refinements only.
